name: Low-Speed Electric Bicycle
description: A two-wheeled bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor that helps only while the rider pedals and stops helping at 20 mph.

restrictions.rule: Two wheels and fully operable pedals; the motor assists only while the rider is pedaling and stops assisting at 20 mph (N.J.S.A. 39:1-1, as amended by P.L.2025, c.285)
The definition sets no motor wattage limit (N.J.S.A. 39:1-1)

An e-bike with a throttle, or with pedal assist past 20 mph up to 28 mph, is a motorized bicycle instead: it also needs a license and registration, must carry liability insurance, and is barred from roads posted over 50 mph
One with pedals and a motor over 750 watts that can exceed 28 mph is an electric motorized bicycle, which the law counts as a motorcycle (N.J.S.A. 39:1-1)
Riders must be 15 or older (P.L.2025, c.285)

Riders need a driver's license or a motorized bicycle (e-bike) license from the Motor Vehicle Commission, which takes a knowledge test and a road test; 15- and 16-year-olds need the e-bike license (P.L.2025, c.285)

Registered with the Motor Vehicle Commission, with its two plate stickers displayed on the front fork; required since July 19, 2026, after a six-month grace period (N.J.S.A. 39:4-14.3i; P.L.2025, c.285)
Riders under 17 must wear a bicycle helmet
Ridden on streets, highways and bicycle paths; a county or municipality may ban it from bicycle paths it controls (N.J.S.A. 39:4-14.16)
May be parked on a sidewalk if it doesn't block pedestrians (N.J.S.A. 39:4-14.16)
Kept off natural-surface trails designated non-motorized unless the local authority allows it (N.J.S.A. 39:4-14.16)
Selling a kit that converts it into a motorized or electric motorized bicycle is prohibited (N.J.S.A. 39:4-14.16)
Not a motor vehicle; the laws that apply to bicycles otherwise apply to it (N.J.S.A. 39:1-1, 39:4-14.16)
A bike-share rider 16 or older needs no license, and the rider doesn't register a shared e-bike (P.L.2025, c.285)
